In this teaching, 'רֵעֲךָ' occupies the evil pole — it is redefined to mean suffering/affliction, not the neighbor-friend of the conventional reading. The polarity evil reflects what this word means within the bechina of Torah #165, not its conventional meaning.

additions.reason: The verse-word 'כָּמוֹךָ' (as yourself, Leviticus 19:18) is the grammatical anchor of the teaching's second bechina chain. In line 4, the Rebbe reinterprets this word: 'כִּי כָּמוֹךָ – כְּמוֹ שֶׁאַתָּה הוּא, הַיְנוּ לְפִי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ.' The verse-word IS redefined as meaning 'as you truly are, according to your deeds.' The polarity is neutral: this is a structural-measure concept, neither holy nor profane — it is the divine justice calculus that determines the proportion between deeds and deserved consequences.

In line 5, the Rebbe reinterprets the verse-phrase 'אֲנִי ה'' with the declaration: 'אֲנִי ה' – בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים.' The dash construction equates 'אֲנִי ה'' with its new meaning: I, God, AM the Master of Mercy. 'בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים' is the substantive theological concept being declared — the divine quality of mercy-mastery. This is the dominant node of Package 3. The entire teaching's comfort-message rests on this bechina: because God IS essentially mercy (IS the Master of Mercy), even the afflictions people receive are expressions of mercy (less than deserved). The concept 'רַחֲמִים' (mercy) also appears in line 2 ('מִתְנַהֵג עִמְּךָ בְּרַחֲמִים') and line 5 ('עֲדַיִן אֲנִי מִתְנַהֵג עִמְּךָ בְּרַחֲמִים'), confirming that mercy-governance is the teaching's positive telos.

The verse-phrase 'אֲנִי ה'' (I am God, Leviticus 19:18) is the grammatical anchor of the teaching's third bechina. In line 5, the Rebbe's reinterpretation declares it IS 'בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים' — God here functions not merely as a divine signature but as the identifying declaration of God's essential quality in this context: I who speak this verse AM the Master of Mercy. The polarity is good: the divine name in this context anchors the positive, merciful dimension of divine governance. The name 'ה'' (the Tetragrammaton) is in Kabbalistic tradition the name associated with mercy (rachamim), which aligns exactly with the teaching's identification of this name with 'בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים'.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: This is the teaching's central practical instruction — 'שֶׁתְּקַבֵּל בְּאַהֲבָה כָּל הָרָעוֹת וְהַיִּסּוּרִין הַבָּאִים עָלֶיךָ' (line 2). The phrase 'שֶׁתְּקַבֵּל בְּאַהֲבָה' describes what one SHOULD DO with the afflictions, not what the afflictions ARE. This is eitza language — the imperative form ('תְּקַבֵּל') is the practical directive that flows from the teaching. There is no 'הַיְנוּ' or dash-reinterpretation declaring that קַבָּלַת יִסּוּרִין IS a bechina of something. Excluded as eitza.

The word 'love' appears as a verb ('וְאָהַבְתָּ', 'שֶׁתֶּאֱהוֹב') in the verse and the teaching's imperative, but it is never declared to BE a bechina of anything. The teaching does not say 'love IS [something]'; it says 'love the evil.' The word 'אַהֲבָה' is the modality of the instruction, not a concept receiving bechina-identification. Excluded.
